recentItems.title: ZELENSKYY, TRUMP, AND PUTIN AT THE SAME TABLE? US prepares talks as Russian economy cracks
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian long-range strikes are hitting Russia's military and economic resources with increasing intensity. Refineries, an airfield, drone storage facilities, and a Wildberries logistics center have come under attack, while fuel shortages force Moscow to extend diesel export restrictions and import aviation fuel. Meanwhile, CIA Director John Ratcliffe has proposed a potential meeting between Zelenskyy, Trump, and Putin. In parallel, Europe warns of the risk of new Russian provocations against NATO and prepares to step up sanctions against the Kremlin.

recentItems.title: CATASTROPHIC LOSSES: Russia loses 40k troops in August! Ukraine to produce SCALP missiles
recentItems.description:
The Russian army is losing more troops in a single month than it can recruit, with losses in August alone exceeding 40,000 personnel. At the same time, Ukrainian forces are stepping up strikes on Russian military facilities, logistics, and oil refining infrastructure, with drones now reaching distances over 1,500 km. In this episode, we break down the situation on the frontline, the impact of these strikes on the Russian economy and fuel sector, the capabilities of Storm Shadow and SCALP missiles, as well as Russia's struggles with army recruitment and the prospects of a new mobilization wave. Discover how these factors are crippling Russia's offensive capabilities.

recentItems.title: WILL NATO SURRENDER THE BALTICS? Former British Officer on where Russia will cross the red line
recentItems.description:
The secret visit of CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Moscow has raised more questions than answers. Military expert and former British Army officer Glen Grant analyzes the potential reasons behind the talks with the FSB and explains how real the threat of a direct confrontation between Russia and NATO truly is. Is the Alliance ready to defend the Baltic states if Moscow crosses the border? We also discuss a potential new mobilization of 600,000 Russians, its blow to the Russian economy, the Kremlin’s manpower struggles, and the risk of a renewed offensive on Kyiv from the north.

recentItems.description:

Plans involve producing enough drones to potentially execute at least 1,000 strikes daily — targeting not only Russian war economy assets, but also critical infrastructure. We analyze how this could alter the course of the war, what to expect from a new Russian mobilization, and what capabilities it will provide to the Kremlin. Also, the main question: is Putin capable of attempting another large-scale offensive against Kyiv?
